chunks: Have you not seen those to whom it was said: 'Restrain your hands (from fighting) and establish prayer and give zakat?'
So when fighting was prescribed for them, behold, a faction of them feared men as with the fear of Allah or with even greater fear.
And they said: 'Our Lord, why have You decreed upon us fighting? Why did You not delay us for a short time?'
Say: 'The enjoyment of the worldly life is little, and the Hereafter is better for him who fears Allah; and you will not be wronged even as much as a thread's breadth.'
ai.seo_question: Why did the Hypocrites hesitate to fight in the battle of Uhud according to the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to illustrate the spiritual fragility of the Munafiqun, whose fear of worldly consequences (like death or loss of status) outweighed their fear of Allah, leading to their hesitation during the Battle of Badr or Hudaybiyyah. The phrase 'no one is wronged even slightly' (fatilan) emphasizes divine justice, while the contrast between 'little enjoyment' and 'superiority for the pious' underscores the transient nature of dunya versus the eternal reward of the Akhirah. This passage serves as a critical lesson on the sincerity of faith, where true piety is measured by readiness to sacrifice for God rather than calculating worldly gains.
